title: Ulysses and the Lotus-Eaters

scope.description: A storm drives Ulysses to the Lotus-Eaters, where scouts eat lotus and forget home.

evidence.sourceText: Three of Ulysses' best men were sent ashore to reconnoiter: but they had not gone very far before they met the natives, seated under their favorite trees, banqueting on their sweet food.
Three of Ulysses' best men were sent ashore to reconnoiter: but they had not gone very far before they met the natives, seated under their favorite trees, banqueting on their sweet food.

The vessels, with broken masts and torn sails, were driven far out of their course, and, after ten days, reached the land of the Lotophagi or Lotus-eaters,--a people whose sole food consisted of lotus fruit and blossoms.

The vessels, with broken masts and torn sails, were driven far out of their course, and, after ten days, reached the land of the Lotophagi or Lotus-eaters,--a people whose sole food consisted of lotus fruit and blossoms.

These received the strangers hospitably, and made them partake of the lotus blossoms; but no sooner had the three men done so, than all recollection of their waiting companions or distant homes passed from their minds, while a dreamy, lethargic sensation stole over them, and made them long to recline there and feast forever.
